back: The focus is the point underground where the rock breaks; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it.
Magnitude = the energy released at the source (one value per earthquake). Intensity = the effects at a place (Modified Mercalli scale I–XII), which varies with distance and local conditions.
Logarithmic: each whole number is about 10 times the wave amplitude and about 32 times the energy.
P waves: fastest, pass through solids and liquids. S waves: slower, solids only. Love and Rayleigh waves: surface waves, slowest but do most damage.
Distance = lag ÷ (1/vS − 1/vP). With vP = 6.0 km/s and vS = 3.5 km/s, distance = 8.4 km × lag in seconds.
Ground shaking, liquefaction, landslides, tsunami, fire and aftershocks.
Haiti (magnitude 7.0, January 2010): estimates of over 100 000 deaths. Chile (magnitude 8.8, February 2010): about 500 deaths. Vulnerability explains the contrast.
Higher where buildings are weak, population density and poverty are high, warning and emergency services are poor, and governance is weak.
v = √(g d). In 4 000 m of water about 198 m/s (about 710 km/h); the wave slows and builds up as the water shallows.
